title: $20,000 instant asset write-off made permanent
headline: Small businesses with turnover under $10m can immediately deduct each asset costing under $20,000, permanently, from 1 July 2026.
summary: The $20,000 instant asset write-off for small businesses is now permanent instead of being renewed one year at a time. Without the change, the threshold would have fallen back to $1,000 on 1 July 2026.

history.note: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 2) Act 2026, No. 71

bigStat.caption: per asset, deducted in the year you start using it

shift.from: Renewed one year at a time

before: The $20,000 threshold was extended a year at a time and would have fallen back to $1,000 on 1 July 2026.
after: Small businesses with aggregated turnover under $10 million can immediately deduct each asset costing less than $20,000 that is first used or installed ready for use from 1 July 2026.
The small business pool's low-value threshold is also permanently $20,000, and the lock-out rule is suspended until 30 June 2027.
exemptions: Businesses with aggregated turnover of $10 million or more.
Assets costing $20,000 or more, which go into the small business pool instead.

actions.text: Keep invoices showing each asset's cost and the date it was first used or installed ready for use.
